decoded.meaning: FWD{ op=READ, dst=/sensor/temp, src=/reply-ep } with an ANCHORLESS relative root stamp — RFC-0025 §4.2.1 (Amendment 1) clause 4, Q10: TF=1 is RESERVED grammar, not removed. The body is byte-identical to fwd/fwd-read; the whole diff is the opt byte (0x40 -> 0x62) and the four trailer bytes, so anything a core does differently with this file is about TF=1 and nothing else.
decoded.note: RFC-0004 §B/§C canonical FWD body; the length field excludes the trailer, as always. TF narrows the trailer timestamp field from 8 bytes to 4 — a signed i32 LE. The value is deliberately NEGATIVE: a core that read the four bytes as u32 would re-emit this file verbatim and still record 4294717296 instead of -250000, so the bound tests assert the DECODED value rather than the round-trip.

tf1_rules.1_decode: A decoder MUST record the relative flag and its delta and SUCCEED. A TF=1 root is well-formed grammar, never a reject. Bound: core/tests/op_resolve_test.cpp — test_tf1_reserved_root.
tf1_rules.2_relay: A relay MUST carry a TF=1 frame verbatim: the forwarding rebuild re-heads the frame (dst shrinks, src grows) but the trailer window — opt bits AND bytes, in the width TF names — crosses the hop untouched. Bound: core/tests/fwd_multihop_test.cpp, over live links.
tf1_rules.3_echo_declines: The #1109 reply-echo path MUST decline a TF=1 root: it is anchorless, so echoing it would propagate a meaningless value. The reply carries NO trailer at all — indistinguishable from what an unstamped request gets. Declining is not an error; the frame still resolves and still answers. Bound: core/tests/op_resolve_test.cpp — test_tf1_reserved_root.
tf1_rules.4_writer_gated: The reference writer does not MINT TF=1. Under the three-clock model (Amendment 1 §4.2.1) the trailer carries WIRE/TX time only, on the outermost frame only, always TF=0; SAMPLE time is a payload TIME (0x0C) child inside the value; PLAYOUT is never transmitted. TF=1 is additive future surface this RFC does not use, not surface it deletes.
